mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Discovery 200Tdi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Land Rover Discovery 200Tdi engine typically costs between £1,800 and £3,000 for supply only, with fully rebuilt, period-correct options ranging from £2,500 to £4,500.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Land Rover Discovery 200Tdi and 300Tdi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 200Tdi (1989-1994) features a Bosch VE rotary injection pump and an earlier block design, while the 300Tdi (1994+) introduced an electronic distributor pump and revised ancillaries.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of head gasket failure in a Land Rover Discovery 200Tdi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs include unexplained coolant loss, a "mayonnaise" substance under the oil filler cap, or white exhaust smoke.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Land Rover Discovery 200Tdi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the rising classic market values of the Discovery 1 (typically £4,000-£12,000+), a rebuild is highly financially viable.

mainEntity.name: How do I verify the exact engine code for my Land Rover Discovery 200Tdi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The engine number is typically stamped on the left-hand side of the cylinder block, near the fuel injection pump.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Discovery 200Tdi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 200Tdi variant launched in the original Discovery 1, it provided a much-needed modern direct-injection turbo-diesel option, replacing aging naturally aspirated units and establishing the blueprint for Land Rover's future off-road capability.

milestones.description: 200Tdi (2.5L Turbo Diesel), 111hp, introduced with the launch of the Discovery 1, featuring a Bosch VE rotary injection pump and an aluminium cylinder head.
Replaced by the 300Tdi engine alongside the Discovery 1 facelift, concluding the original 200Tdi production run after five years of service.

problems.rootCause: Ageing gasket materials and the thermal expansion differences between the cast-iron block and aluminium cylinder head lead to weeping, coolant loss, and eventual head gasket failure.
